concepts.title: Sierpinski Carpet: Remaining Squares
concepts.definition: Split a square into 9 equal parts, blank the centre one, and repeat the split-and-blank inside every survivor.
concepts.key_idea: The number of squares grows exponentially by a factor of 8 at each iteration.
question_patterns: How many squares remain in the Sierpinski Carpet at step n?
Calculate the number of remaining squares after 3 iterations.
Find the value of Rn for the nth step of a Sierpinski Carpet.
How many squares remain after 2 rounds?
Survivor count at step 4 of the carpet?

solution_steps.explain: The step number n represents the iteration of the fractal process.
Since each square splits into 8 remaining squares, we raise 8 to the power of n.

solution_steps.action: State the final count of remaining squares
solution_steps.explain: The value of 8^n gives the exact number of survivor squares after n iterations of the split-and-blank process.

concepts.title: Sierpinski Carpet: Total Holes
concepts.definition: Count every blank pocket dug into the carpet so far.
concepts.key_idea: Each round digs 8^n new pockets; pockets total (8^n - 1)/7.
question_patterns: Find the number of holes in the Sierpinski Carpet at step n.
How many square holes are formed after n steps?
Calculate Hn for the Sierpinski Carpet.
How many pockets after 2 rounds?
Total holes after 3 rounds?

solution_steps.explain: Subtract 1 from 8 raised to the power of n.
Divide the result by 7 to get the total number of holes.

solution_steps.action: State the final count of total holes
solution_steps.explain: The geometric sum (8^n - 1)/7 accumulates every blank pocket dug across all n rounds of the carpet process.

concepts.title: Sierpinski Gasket: Remaining Triangles
concepts.definition: Split a triangle into 4 equal parts, take out the centre one, and repeat on every survivor.
concepts.key_idea: Every round triples the survivors: 3^n after n rounds.
question_patterns: How many triangles remain in the Sierpinski Gasket at step n?
Calculate the number of small triangles after n iterations.
Find the count of triangles in the nth step of the Sierpinski Triangle.
Triangles after 3 rounds?
Survivor triangles at step 2?

solution_steps.explain: Each step keeps 3 out of 4 triangles from the previous step.
The step number n counts how many rounds of split-and-remove-centre have been performed on the starting triangle.

solution_steps.action: State the final count of remaining triangles
solution_steps.explain: The value of 3^n gives the exact number of survivor triangles after n rounds of the gasket process.

concepts.title: Koch Snowflake: Number of Sides
concepts.definition: Count the straight pieces edging the snowflake curve after n rounds.
concepts.key_idea: Every single side is replaced by four smaller segments in each subsequent step.
question_patterns: Find the number of sides in the nth step of the Koch Snowflake.
How many segments make up the Koch Snowflake at step n?
Calculate the side count for a Koch fractal after n iterations.
Edge pieces after 2 rounds?
How many segments at step 3?

solution_steps.explain: Each original side becomes 4 sides in one step, so for n steps it is 4^n.
The snowflake starts with an equilateral triangle (3 sides).
The product 3 x 4^n gives the exact number of straight segments edging the snowflake after n rounds.

concepts.title: Koch Snowflake: Perimeter
concepts.definition: The total length of the outer boundary of the Koch Snowflake, assuming the initial triangle side length is 1.
concepts.key_idea: The perimeter increases by a factor of 4/3 at every step, leading to an infinite length in the limit.
question_patterns: What is the perimeter of the Koch Snowflake at step n?
Find the total boundary length of the snowflake after n steps.
Calculate the perimeter if the starting side length is 1 unit.
Perimeter after 2 rounds starting from side 1?
Boundary length at step 3, start side 1?

solution_steps.explain: The perimeter grows by 4/3 each step.
The initial perimeter of a triangle with side 1 is 3.
The product 3 x (4/3)^n gives the total boundary length of the snowflake after n rounds, starting from side length 1.

concepts.title: Properties of Prisms
concepts.definition: A solid with two identical polygonal bases and rectangular or parallelogram lateral faces.
concepts.key_idea: Base decides all: F = n + 2, V = 2n, E = 3n.
question_patterns: How many faces does a prism with an n-sided base have?
Calculate the number of edges and vertices for a pentagonal prism.
Find F, V, and E for a prism where the base has n sides.
Faces of a pentagonal prism?
Count F, V, E of a hexagonal prism.

solution_steps.explain: Two bases plus n side faces.
n vertices on the top base and n on the bottom.
n edges on each base and n connecting edges.

concepts.title: Properties of Pyramids
concepts.definition: One polygonal floor with triangular walls rising to a single point.
concepts.key_idea: The number of faces and vertices are equal in any pyramid.
question_patterns: Find the number of vertices in a pyramid with an n-sided base.
How many edges does a hexagonal pyramid have?
Calculate F, V, and E for a pyramid with base sides n.
Vertices of a hexagonal pyramid?
Edges of a pentagonal pyramid?

solution_steps.explain: One base plus n triangles (faces) or n base points plus one apex (vertices).
n base edges plus n edges connecting to the apex.
Check that F + V - E = 2 holds for the pyramid, confirming the counts are consistent.

concepts.title: Shortest Path on Cuboid Surface
concepts.definition: Flatten the box faces into a plane; the straight line there is the shortest trip over the surface.
concepts.key_idea: Unfold, draw straight, then measure -- the flat shortcut is the surface shortcut.
question_patterns: What is the shortest path for an ant to travel on a box?

Calculate the shortest surface distance using the Baudhayana theorem.
Ant on a 3x2x1 box, corner to opposite corner -- shortest walk?
Shortest surface trip on a 4x2x1 box, corner to corner?

solution_steps.explain: Identify the total horizontal and vertical displacement on the unfolded net.
Square the vertical distance.
The shortest path is the square root of the sum of squares.

concepts.title: Solid Projections: Front, Top, and Side Views
concepts.definition: Picture the object from straight ahead, above, and the side; draw each flat outline.
concepts.key_idea: Each viewpoint gives one flat profile; together they pin the solid down.
question_patterns: Identify the top view of the given solid.
Draw the front, side, and top views of a cylinder.
Match the solid with its projections.
Sketch the top view of a brick.
Which view shows the circular face of a can?

solution_steps.explain: Look at the object directly at eye level to find the front profile.
Look at the object from a bird's-eye view to find the top profile.
Look at the object from the left or right to find the side profile.
